The report now shows `REORDER` for any item whose stock on hand is less than 6 days' worth of average sales. `LEAD_TIME_DAYS = 6` sits at the top of `stock_report.py` for when you switch suppliers.

I ran it against your current `inventory.csv`:

```
SKU      ITEM                       ON HAND  STATUS
CF-1K    House blend 1kg                  9  REORDER
CF-250   Colombia beans 250g             42  ok
FL-100   Paper filters x100               0  OUT
MG-12    Enamel mug                      18  ok
OT-1L    Oat milk 1L                     30  REORDER
TE-50    Breakfast tea x50               25  ok
```

House blend has 9 on hand against 14.4 needed (2.4 a day for 6 days), and oat milk has 30 against 45.

- **Exact cover counts as ok:** an item with exactly 6 days of stock left is not flagged, since it runs out just as the delivery lands. In practice that means the flag appears the night stock first dips below 6 days' worth, so an order placed then can still leave the shelf empty for up to a day. Raising `LEAD_TIME_DAYS` to 7 gives you a day of cushion.
- **Empty shelves still show `OUT`:** items at zero keep the `OUT` status rather than `REORDER`, so you can tell the two apart.
